answers.children: Sloughis are moderately good with children. Their reserved nature and independent streak mean they bond closely with one or two people but can be aloof or wary around noisy or unpredictable youngsters, a trait rooted in their history as desert hunters that lived intimately with nomadic families yet retained quiet dignity. Owners must provide space so the dog can retreat when overstimulated, preventing stress for both. (PawLabs child-friendly score: 5/10)
answers.other-pets: Sloughis do not always get along with other pets. Their strong sighthound prey drive, honed for chasing gazelle and hare across North African deserts, makes small animals risky while same-sex tension can arise from their independent temperament. Careful introductions are essential if another dog shares the home, as the Sloughi tends to focus on its own priorities rather than pack sociability.
answers.exercise: Sloughis need at least an hour of exercise daily. Short intense sprints in a securely fenced area suit their exceptional speed and agility as desert hunters better than steady endurance work, after which they settle for long naps indoors. Without this release their independent nature leads to restlessness, pacing or fixation on movement outside windows.
answers.shedding: No — Sloughis shed lightly year-round. Their short smooth single coat lacks the density or feathering of heavier sighthounds so loose hair is minimal and easy to wipe away, yet the sleek texture still shows every speck of desert dust tracked in from outside runs. Daily brushing keeps the coat gleaming with little effort.
answers.hypoallergenic: No breed is truly hypoallergenic and the Sloughi is not commonly suggested for allergy sufferers. Its short smooth coat produces some dander despite low shedding, a consequence of the lean desert build that prioritises speed over insulation. Allergy testing before adopting remains the only reliable gauge.
answers.training: Sloughis are not easy to train. Their independent and reserved temperament, shaped by centuries of hunting gazelle without constant human direction, produces stubbornness and selective listening rather than eager biddability. Sensitivity to tone means harsh methods backfire, so patient work that respects their quiet dignity yields the best results.
answers.lifespan: Sloughis live 12-15 years. Their lean athletic build and history of endurance chases across harsh North African terrain support a robust frame that contributes to this range, with the breed maintaining quiet dignity and agility well into later years when given appropriate outlets.
answers.size: Sloughis reach 35-50 lb and stand 24-29 in tall. The sleek, lightly built frame feels elegant rather than bulky in the home, with long legs and a streamlined body that lets them curl compactly on a bed yet still fill a room with their quiet presence when standing alert.
answers.barking: Sloughis do not bark much. Bred as silent hunters of swift game in open desert, they remain quiet unless something truly demands attention, their reserved nature favouring watchful stillness over vocal alerts. This low tendency suits owners who value peace but means they rarely announce visitors.
answers.apartment: Sloughis can live in an apartment. Their calm indoor settling, low barking and short smooth coat that leaves little mess fit smaller homes, provided daily sprint sessions occur elsewhere to satisfy the energy and prey drive of this North African sighthound. Without secure outdoor access they become restless.
answers.first-time: Sloughis are not a good first dog. Their aloofness with strangers, independent decision-making and need for an owner who respects their reserved dignity create demands that challenge novices, especially when the dog ignores recall to scan for imaginary prey during walks.
